fields.acceptance: make check runs a Go source scan that pins machine.toml to internal/machine, which only reads it, and a testscript showing the ops that read trust leave machine.toml byte-identical and never create it
fields.statement: Rhiza never writes or raises a machine's trust: the machine config is changed only by hand, so no agent, run or daemon can lift the bypass refusal through rhiza.

ops.note: Never writing trust keeps the dedicated-only bypass rule from being lifted by rhiza itself

fields.acceptance: (1) A Go test parses the module's non-test Go source (go/parser) and fails if internal/machine calls any file-writing or file-changing function (os.WriteFile, os.Create, os.OpenFile with write flags, os.Mkdir/MkdirAll, os.Rename, os.Remove/RemoveAll, os.Chmod, os.Symlink/Link, os.Truncate), if internal/machine exports anything but Path, Read, Load, Config and the trust constants, or if any file outside internal/machine names the machine config file other than as a display string (no filepath.Join or open of "machine.toml"). (2) A testscript sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME, writes machine.toml with trust = "daily" and keeps a copy, runs rhiza machine show, rhiza api call machine.show, rhiza health and the refused rhiza session start --permission-mode bypassPermissions, then cmp shows the file byte-identical and trust still daily; a second pass with no machine config runs the same ops and the file still does not exist.
fields.statement: make check proves no rhiza code path writes the machine config: the file is reached only through internal/machine, which can only read it, and the ops that read trust leave it unchanged
